listingTitle: Avoid flushing C++ streams in loops
title: Avoid flushing C++ streams in loops
why: std::endl writes a newline and flushes the stream, so repeated use in a loop can force unnecessary I/O synchronization.
suggestion: Write a newline character and flush explicitly only where the program requires immediate output.
limitations: Only explicit std::endl references inside braced for, while, or do loops are reported.
Aliases, macros, required interactive flushing, and loop trip counts are not inferred.
